l.i: An Petrus fuerit Pontifex Oecumenicus, & Caput Ec-

main_text.l: clesiæ, ac Vicarius Christi? Neg. cont. Pontif.
I. Licèt.præcedens Quæstio vanitatem Pontificatus œcumenici in
thesi demonstraverit. Quia tamen Adversarii eum adstruere
conantur variis argumentis in hypothesi respectu Petri, & Pontificum
Romanorum, qui dicuntur ejus Successores, peculiari Controversia de
hoc argumento disputandum est; ut veritas adversus mendacium plenè
confirmetur.
II. Circa Statum Quæstionis observamus, 1. Non quæri de Primatu
quocunque, vel ordinis, & vocationis, vel ætatis, vel dignitatis, & donorum.
Non negamus enim Primatum istum Petro posse competere, sive quia
primus vocatus erat à Christo, ut liquet ex Matt. 4. 18. & sic ordine pri-
mus erat, ut sæpe fieri solet inter eos qui potestate sunt pares ad vitandam
confusionem, quo sensu dicitur primus Matth. 10. 2. sive ratione
donorum & dignitatis, quomodo Nicodemus vocatur ἄρχων τῶν Ἰουδαίων
Joan. 3. 1. non quòd Judæis imperaret, sed quia magna erat illi apud Ju-
dæos authoritas, sic Gamaliel dicitur τίμιος [illegible, ~5 letters] τῷ λαῷ Act. 5. 34.

page.notes: Ink is faded and the scan is blurred at the right edge, so the marginal notes and the Greek are uncertain. The Greek in Act. 5. 34 has an illegible middle word. The Greek in Joan. 3. 1 is read as printed, with [?] not added. The title "Status Quæstionis" note has a small mark before it that could not be identified. The printed Hebrew-like abbreviation "Hosè" is read as Hose. The page's main-text line "Licèt.præcedens" is printed without a space. Text spelling is kept as printed, including "non eris finis" as shown in the scan. The printed "Ezech." in the text and "Ezec." in the margin are both copied as they appear.
